questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Location, language, student-city

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: yes, the coordinator had made a "how to" doucment for us. However, it could use some updates.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Introduction by the coordinator, but I was also a lot on my own i would say. Luckily we made a group chat so that we could assist each other.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: CROUS - there were no options, we just got a room. For the price and location and considering that many of my fellow exchanger students were there it was good!

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Meals for both lunch and dinner for 3,30 EUR is a great deal!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Bring kitchenware and be aware that its not only lunch but also dinner thats available! Dinner is in the Crouzzeria if youre in Cuques housing.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: For the price it was great.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I feel it could be better bureacracy-wise, but it works. Also, the coordinator makes sure to remind you if anything is missing.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It all worked through emails from the coordinator sending us links, etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email of the erasmus-coordinator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted, no problem whatsoever. Its all lectures so there are no real limits for erasmus students (at least from my experience).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it in time and take your time. Also remember, that you can always change courses!!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The system is just different but the exams are doable. The professors take into consideration that french isnt your first language (if that is what you do).

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Every course was 6 ECTS, but this does not mean that there wasnt a lot of information. Especially for the french courses it was sometimes challenging to follow everything the professor said because of the language barrier. The courses I attended were more knowledge based, and not so much method (also because erasmus students dont fo the "travaux dirigees" where papers are submitted). I would say the level is good - not too easy but if you study in reasonable time before the exams it works.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Completely different. No reading list, no trial-assignments - youre very much on your own. I liked that it was different,but prefer the methods at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Terminologie juridique
Ordre juridique approfondi de l'Union européenne 
Espace judiciaire Européen

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Espace judiciaire Européen was my favourite. Good professors, and a cool insight into how the judicial cooperation is within the EU on civil and penal matters.

Housing DKK per month *

Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not unexpected but I took some trips! So I would put money on the side for that.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I expected food to be cheaper than it was. Clothes are less expensive and obviously the housing. A good surprise was the canteens!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I attended swimming and koduro fit. there is also a choir. Moreover i attended ESN events that were nice as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join ESN events, take advantage of the campus-festivals.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Nice, Menton, Cassis for hiking. Marseille is always lovely.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The first days are a little challenging, but as soon as you find some people everything becomes amazing and it goes by so fast. ENJOY IT!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Erasmus Student Network (ESN) events, make a group chat with the other students you meet, get a french buddy (the Erasmus coordinator facilitates that).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sometimes the french can be a bit harsh, but usually theyre nice!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Food, the laissez-faire culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- be open-minded 
- seize opportunities
- help each other and be there for each other (meaning the other exchange students)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If youre having challenges with the erasmus coordinator sometimes, be patient, youre not the only one. If you live in a dorm, the kitchens are not the best but think of the prize! Yes, study but also, if you start a moth before exams youll be more than fine.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The self-development, getting better at french, meeting people from all over and maybe even friends for life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The part in the beginning where I didnt have any social connections. Its weird suddently going from a place where theres always stuff to do and then having "nothing". But that changes within a week and then its great! Also doing daily life things in french, like speaking to someone in a store is also a good challenge but that just makes you better!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
